title: What Makes Japanese Customer Service Unique
paragraphs: Japan is famous around the world for its excellent customer service. Many visitors are surprised by how polite and helpful workers are in shops, hotels and restaurants. So what makes Japanese customer service so special?
Japanese customer service is often connected to a word: "omotenashi." It means Japanese hospitality, or the Japanese way of welcoming and taking care of guests.

One important part of omotenashi is that it is done without expecting anything in return. In many countries, workers may hope to get a tip for good service. But in Japan, tipping is not common. Good service is simply part of the job.

Another important part is thinking ahead. Workers try to understand what customers need before the customers ask. In this way, they try to solve problems before they happen. In many other countries, customer service often waits for a customer to complain first, and then tries to fix the problem.

Omotenashi also comes from Japanese culture and history. Many people describe it as an old Japanese way of thinking, in which a person serves a guest with all their heart and without thinking of themselves.
Good service in Japan is not only about people. It can also be about systems and design that make customers feel comfortable.
The Japanese government also promotes omotenashi as a special part of Japanese culture. It has even trained hotels and other tourism businesses in its ideas.
